# MASTER PUBLIC LORE: What Every Kythorian Knows

This document aggregates all PUBLIC, WIDELY-AVAILABLE knowledge that an average citizen of Kythoria would possess. All secret lore (GM-only, divine conspiracy, hidden organizations, true origins) is excluded. This represents the common understanding of the world as taught in schools, preached in temples, and discussed in taverns.

---

## 1. THE WORLD: AETRIS

### 1.1 Name and Nature
- The world is called **Aetris** -- an ancient name evoking both "aeon" and "triad"
- Aetris contains **three known continents**
- The campaign takes place on the continent of **Kythoria**
- The other two continents exist but are distant and scarcely known

### 1.2 Planes (Basic Cosmology)
- Beyond the material world exist other planes of reality
- The **Inner Planes** are realms of raw elemental forces (Fire, Water, Earth, Air)
- The **Outer Planes** are the domains of the gods and other powerful beings
- The **Feywild** and **Shadowfell** are known as realms of fey and shadow
- The **Astral Plane** connects all planes and allows planar travel
- The **Ethereal Plane** is a misty realm that overlaps the material world

### 1.3 Ley Lines
- Invisible highways of concentrated magical energy crisscross the world
- Where ley lines converge, magic is easier to channel and more powerful
- The capital city **Weaveheart** is built at a major ley line convergence

---

## 2. THE CONTINENT OF KYTHORIA

### 2.1 Climate & Regions

#### The Frozen North (Arctic / Subarctic)
- Harsh, cold expanse of tundra, taiga, and snow-capped mountains
- Before the invasion, hardy dwarf holds and human settlements dotted this region
- Today, much of the north remains under monster control
- Rumors speak of sentient blizzards and cold-adapted horrors

#### The Temperate Heartlands
- Four distinct seasons; fertile farmlands, rolling hills, and dense forests
- The most densely populated and safest region
- Home to the three capital cities: **Skywatch**, **Emberforge**, **Weaveheart**

#### The Subtropical South
- Warm climate with mild winters, long summers, and abundant rainfall
- Dense jungles, mangrove swamps, and white-sand beaches
- One of the first regions fully recovered
#### The Eastern Coast & Sea Routes
- Vital artery for inter-continental trade and travel
- Safe sea lanes connect major ports between south. east and northeast
- Recovered early in the reconquering; thriving network of port towns and fishing villages

#### The Western Frontier
- Contested zone marking the boundary between reclaimed territory and monster-held lands
- Rugged highlands, deep forests, and the unknown reaches of the far west
- Dotted with military outposts, forward operating bases, and fledgling settlements

### 2.2 Current Territorial Control
- Approximately **two-thirds of the continent** has been reclaimed
- The recovered south and east host thriving settlements, farms, and trade routes
- Some part of the north and west remain contested
- Approximately **one-third** of the continent remains under monster control

### 2.3 Map Features (Known)
- The continent spans from frozen northern reaches to subtropical southern shores
- A **major forward operating base** serves as the Last Stand army's command center for reconquering operations on the western frontier
- **Two major sea ports**: one in the southeast (heavily fortified, highly defensible) and one in the east


---

## 3. HISTORY: THE THREE ERAS

### 3.1 Era of Foundation (Before ~500 Years Ago)
- The age of the **Six Mortal Kingdoms**
- Much has been lost to time; few records survive
- Knowledge is pieced together from fragments of ancient texts, ruins, and oral traditions

#### The Six Kingdoms

| Kingdom               | Race      | Capital    | Known For                                                            |
| --------------------- | --------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Kingdom of Drakhaven  | Humans    | Drakhaven  | Largest and most advanced city; self-appointed "capital of Kythoria" |
| Kingdom of Elyndor    | Elves     | Elyndor    | Ancient forest capital of arcane knowledge                           |
| Kingdom of Kazadur    | Dwarves   | Kazadur    | Mountain-forge capital; greatest mines on the continent              |
| Kingdom of Hearthglen | Halflings | Hearthglen | Agricultural heartland; home of the royal mint                       |
| Kingdom of Everquill  | Gnomes    | Everquill  | Scholarly capital of law, records, and maps                          |
| Kingdom of Stonefist  | Half-Orcs | Stonefist  | Rugged fortress capital of proud warriors                            |

- Uncommon races (Genasi, Dragonborn, Tieflings) had no kingdom; they grouped together in large villages
- A great overland trade route called **Crassian's Dust Circle** connected all six kingdoms
- Raw metals from Kazadur's mines were shipped to Hearthglen for minting into currency
- Hearthglen and Everquill made the first business treaty that introduced currency in Kythoria
### 3.2 The Abominable End (~400 to ~200 Years Ago)
- Approximately **400 years ago**, an ever-growing tide of monsters began appearing at the fringes of Kythoria
- Their numbers were relentless; origins were unknown
- For two centuries, war plagued the continent - The Undying Scurge War, countless died, civilizations crumbled
- The initial pace of conquering was ruthless and accelarated
- As time went by, the pace became slowed and slughish
- Five incredibly powerfull beings came to be known as the **Five Monster Generals**
- All six kingdoms fell, cities were overrun, and the mortal races were pushed to the brink of extinction
- This era is remembered as a time of unimaginable cruelty and suffering

### 3.3 The Rise of the Mortals (~200 Years Ago to Present)

#### The Founding of the Last Stand
- Approximately **200 years ago**, the surviving mortal races made their final stand near the center-southeast of the continent
- Three capital cities were established: **Skywatch**, **Emberforge**, and **Weaveheart**
- Together, these became known as **the Last Stand**
- A **magical barrier** was developed in Weaveheart, powered by the ley line convergence, creating a safe haven from the monster hordes

#### The First Alliance
- After the capitals were established, the mortal races formed an unprecedented alliance
- Kings, archmages, high priests, ancient monster hunters, and knightly orders united
- The Alliance established the Dawn Guard - the First Alliance's army
- The Dawn Guard waged a reconquering effort spaning multiple decades against the monster army
- **Three of the Five Monster Generals** were defeated
- The remaining two generals retreated and have not been seen since

#### The Reconquering
- From the safety of the Last Stand, the mortal races organized and began pushing back
- Campaigns continue to this day to reclaim the north and west
- The south and east have been fully reclaimed and resettled
- Several monster hoards and nests remaind throughout the reconquered lands
- No one knows what remains in the lands still under rule of the Monster Army


---

## 4. THE THREE CAPITALS (THE LAST STAND)

### 4.1 Skywatch (The Lookout)
- The highest-elevated of the three capital cities
- Capital city for the Elven people
- Perched on elevated terrain with panoramic views
- Serves as the primary **scouting and observation post**
- Keeps constant watch over monster movements and relays intelligence
- Provides military advantage and superiority to the Dawn Guard  over the monster army 
- Favored by those attuned to scouting, vigilance, and ranged combat
- **Governance**: Ruled by a King with the counsel of the **Council of Eyes** (meritocratic scouts, rangers, and strategists)

#### Notable Features
- **Skywatch War College**: Trains fighters, paladins, rangers, and strategic officers
- **Guiding Hand Guild**: Headquarters of the continent's premier scouting organization
- **Cartography Hall**: Maps, scouting reports, and intelligence archives spanning two centuries
- **The Skywatch Chorus**: Famous choir performing at major festivals

### 4.2 Emberforge (The Forge)
- An **underground city** built beneath a volcanic ash wasteland
- Capital city for the Dwarven people
- Harnesses geothermal heat and volcanic resources for industry
- The **industrial heart** of the reconquering effort
- Produces weapons, armor, and equipment for the Dawn Guard
- The geothermal forges allow the smithing of exceptional alloys and metals
- Equipment produced here gives the technological advantage to the Dawn Guard  against the Monster army
- **Governance**: Ruled by a King with the counsel of the **Forgemaster's Circle** (guild leaders, craft clans, engineering houses)

#### Notable Features
- **Volcanic Forges**: Geothermally-powered furnaces reaching temperatures no surface forge can match
- **Engineering Halls**: Premier training grounds for artificers
- **Engineering Archives**: Schematics, metallurgical treatises, and architectural plans
- **The Emberforge Opera**: Dramatic performances combining music, precise engineering, and magical effects

#### Production
- Weapons and armor for the military (considered the finest available)
- Tools for farming, construction, and mining
- Components for arcane research and enchantment
- Unique alloys made possible by volcanic heat and rare ores
- Center for monster-part crafting innovation

### 4.3 Weaveheart (The Nexus)
- Built at the convergence of **multiple ley lines**
- Capital city for Humans
- The **arcane and research heart** of the Last Stand
- Site where the magical barrier was first developed and later expanded to protect all three capitals
- **Governance**: Ruled by a King with the counsel of the **Arcane Conclave** (wizards, scholars, and arcane researchers). Magocracy in practice -- knowledge of the weave translates into political influence.

#### Notable Features
- **Grand Athenaeum**: The largest collection of arcane texts, historical records, and pre-invasion literature on the continent
- **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts**: The continent's premier magical institution
- **The Magical Barrier**: Stable, reliable defensive perimeter protecting all three capitals, constantly maintained by Weaveheart's mages
- **Weaveheart Illuminations**: Magical light shows and illusions for entertainment

### 4.4 The Magical Barrier
- A stable, reliable defensive perimeter capable of keeping monsters at bay
- First developed in Weaveheart using the ley line convergence
- Later expanded to create a perimeter encompassing all three capitals
- Has held for **two centuries**
- Requires constant arcane attention from Weaveheart's mages to maintain

## 5. GOVERNANCE & LAW

### 5.1 The Council Accord (The Three Kings)
- The closest thing to a central authority in mortal civilization
- Each capital has a **King**; the three form the Council Accord
- No fixed schedule; kings gather frequently by tradition
- Any king may invoke a formal council
- Structure ensures no single point of failure -- if one city falls, the others continue

### 5.2 The Survival Code (Foundation Law)
Five Articles applicable across all territories:
- **Life** -- No murder
- **Supply** -- No theft of military resources
- **Allegiance** -- No treason
- **Barrier** -- No sabotage of defenses
- **Truth** -- No false accusations

- Penalties: labor, exile, or execution
- Beyond the Code, each settlement governs itself; a patchwork of local customs

### 5.3 Guild System
Major guilds across the continent:
- **Thalkis Ember**: Metalworkers, artisans
- **Guiding Hand**: Intelligence and frontier navigation
- **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts**: Arcane research and education

- **Sons of Crassian**: Commerce and trade
- Drakh Ix'thar** (Adventurers' Guild): Monster hunting and ruin delving

Each guild provides training, representation, and a social safety net for its members.

### 5.4 Political Landscape
- Political structures are young (~200 years) and still crystallizing
- **Frontier**: 3S's Merit-based leadership - those who have strength, strategy and soul lead
- **Heartland**: Traditional authorities (wealthy families, guilds)
- Authority varies significantly by settlement

### 5.5 Militarized Society

- Every able-bodied citizen is expected to contribute to the reconquering
- The unified army contracts local mercenary groups for specific operations

## 6. RELIGION: THE PANTHEON

### 6.1 The Ten Gods
The mortal races worship a pantheon of ten gods. Each god created a specific mortal race and governs specific domains of existence.

### 6.2 The Seven Recognized Gods

| #   | God          | Domains         |  Church                | Role                                          |
| --- | ------------ | --------------- |  --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Kaelthor** | Nature, Tempest |  Circle of the Wild    | Druids, weather-watchers, frontier folk       |
| 2   | **Aurelius** | Wisdom, Justice |  Order of the Scales   | Judges, scholars, lawkeepers                  |
| 3   | **Vesper**   | Peace, Twilight |  Vigil of the Dusk     | Diplomats, threshold guardians, funeral rites |
| 4   | **Aloria**   | Light, Life     |  Order of the Dawn     | Healers, protectors, midwives                 |
| 5   | **Tyra**     | Hunt, Nature    |  Pack of Tyra          | Hunters, survivalists, trackers               |
| 6   | **Thalkis**  | Forge, Arcana   |  Guild of the Spark    | Smiths, enchanters, artificers                |
| 7   | **Crassian** | Wealth, Fortune |  Order of the Currency | Merchants, bankers, traders                   |

### 6.3 The Three Banned Gods

| #   | God             | Domains       | Church              | Why Banned                  |
| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------- |
| 8   | **Raven Queen** | Death, Grave  | Order of the Raven  | Blamed for monster invasion |
| 9   | **Vorn**        | War, Conquest | Iron Host           | Blamed for monster invasion |
| 10  | **Lolth**       | Trickery, War | Coven of the Spider | Blamed for monster invasion |

- These three gods are publicly blamed for orchestrating the monster invasion
- Their churches are banned from operating openly within Last Stand territories

### 6.4 The Creation Myth
The order in which the gods created the world, according to church teaching:

1. **Kaelthor** shaped the world, planes, and nature from chaos (Month 1)
2. **Aurelius** imposed laws and order upon nature (Month 2)
3. **Vesper** introduced peace, harmony, and boundaries between states (Month 3)
4. **Aloria** brought light and reproduction (Month 4)
5. **Tyra** instilled hunger and survival instinct (Month 5)
6. **Raven Queen** completed the cycle with death and mourning (Month 6)
7. **Thalkis** taught forge and arcane knowledge (Month 7)
8. **Crassian** introduced currency and trade (Month 8)
9. **Vorn** granted the ability to wage war and conquer (Month 9)
10. **Lolth** provided wit and cunning to avoid conflict (Month 10)

### 6.5 The Ecumenical Council
- Interfaith governing body representing the **seven recognized churches**
- Mediates disputes between faiths
- Coordinates major religious festivals
- Meets in a neutral hall in **Weaveheart**
- The three banned churches (Coven of the Spider, Order of the Raven, Iron Host) are excluded

### 6.6 Divine Conflict
- The gods have rivalries, alliances, and conflicts among themselves

- The three banned gods are seen as enemies of the seven recognized gods


### 6.7 Individual God Profiles
#### Kaelthor (Nature & Tempest)
- God of the untamed world: wilderness, storms, beasts, raw natural forces
- Personality: Wild, unpredictable, indifferent to mortal concerns
- Worship: Shrines in wild places rather than cities; the world itself is considered the only true temple
- Followers: Druids, rangers, sailors, farmers

#### Aurelius (Wisdom & Justice)
- God of truth, learning, law, and fair judgment
- Personality: Measured, calm, deliberate
- Worship: Temples double as courts, libraries, and academies
- Followers: Judges, scholars, diplomats, lawkeepers

#### Vesper (Peace & Twilight)
- God of serenity, boundaries, transitions, and the quiet spaces between
- Personality: Serene, patient, diplomatic
- Worship: Quiet sanctuaries of peace; mediators who resolve conflicts
- Followers: Diplomats, hospice workers, gatekeepers

#### Aloria (Light & Life)
- Represented as the benevolent face of the pantheon: healing, compassion, radiance, the life-giving sun
- Personality: Warm, nurturing, protective of mortals
- Worship: Most beloved and trusted god. Temples in all settlements.
- Followers: Healers, midwives, protectors, common folk

#### Tyra (Hunt & Nature)
- God of the hunt, tracking, predator-prey balance, and survival
- Personality: Patient, sharp, instinctual
- Worship: Shrines in the deep wilderness. Clergy are masters of tracking and survival.
- Followers: Rangers, hunters, trackers, scouts

#### Thalkis (Forge & Arcana)
- God of creation through craft and magic; patron of artisans, smiths, and mages
- Personality: Meticulous, creative, patient
- Worship: Temples are workshops, forges, and arcane libraries
- Followers: Smiths, enchanters, artificers

#### Crassian (Wealth & Fortune)
- God of trade, commerce, prosperity, luck, and fate
- Personality: Pragmatic, opportunistic; favors ambition and risk-taking
- Worship: Temples double as banks and marketplaces
- Followers: Traders, moneylenders, gamblers, adventurers

#### Raven Queen (Death & Grave) -- BANNED
- God of death, the grave, and the cycle of life and death
- Personality: Solemn, patient, absolute. Despises undeath.
- Worship: Banned in Last Stand territories; operates in hidden sanctuaries
- Followers: Grave wardens, memory-keepers

#### Vorn (War & Conquest) -- BANNED
- God of war, battle, strategy, conquest, and the glory of victory
- Personality: Bold, commanding, relentless
- Worship: Officially banned; Iron Host operates underground
- Followers: Soldiers, generals, mercenaries (in secret)

#### Lolth, The Spider Queen (Trickery & War) -- BANNED
- God of trickery, war, deception, cunning
- Personality: Manipulative, patient, merciless
- Worship: Banned, operates in hidden sanctuaries 
- Followers: Spies, assassins

## 7. THE CALENDAR & FESTIVALS

### 7.1 Calendar Structure
- **System**: 10 months (named after gods, in creation order)
- **2 weeks per month** = 20 days per month
- **10-day week**: 4 work days / 2 rest days / 3 work days / 1 rest day
- **200 days per year**
- The calendar has existed for approximately **500 years**, established by the first mortal kingdoms

### 7.2 Weekday Names
Wildtide, Lawrest, Duskfall, Life-dawn, Fangrest, Gravefall, Sparktide, Cointide, Warmorn, Shadowrest

### 7.3 Months & Festivals

| Month          | God         | Festival            | Day    | Description                          |
| -------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------ |
| 1. Kaelthor    | Kaelthor    | Harvest Communion   | Day 1  | Feasting, giving thanks              |
| 2. Aurelius    | Aurelius    | The Weighing        | Day 2  | Legal amnesty, oath-renewal          |
| 3. Vesper      | Vesper      | The Dusk Chime      | Day 3  | Hour of silence at sunset            |
| 4. Aloria      | Aloria      | Sunrise Rekindling  | Day 4  | Grand illumination ceremony          |
| 5. Tyra        | Tyra        | The Great Hunt      | Day 5  | Continent-wide hunting competition   |
| 6. Raven Queen | Raven Queen | The Lantern Vigil   | Day 6  | Paper lanterns released for the dead |
| 7. Thalkis     | Thalkis     | The Great Forging   | Day 7  | Craft fair and invention exhibition  |
| 8. Crassian    | Crassian    | Fortune's Gamble    | Day 8  | Markets, gambling, commerce          |
| 9. Vorn        | Vorn        | The Bloody Standard | Day 9  | War games and military parades       |
| 10. Lolth      | Lolth       | Night of Whispers   | Day 10 | Shadowed deals (observed in secret)  |

### 7.4 Day of Silence
- The **last day of the year** (Day 200)
- Secular observance; no work, no magic
- Quiet reflection honoring the dead
- The only festival not tied to any god

## 8. SOCIETY & CULTURE

### 8.1 Core Values
Forged by two centuries of shared struggle:

- **Unity**: "Divided we fight but united we stand" - Racial differences persist in traditions, but a sense of community against a common enemy reigns. No exclusion, no discrimination.
- **Resilience** -- Hardship is met with determination. Stoicism is admired; complaint is seen as weakness; people speak of problems only if they offer solutions
- **Contribution** -- Every citizen is expected to do their part. Laziness is heavily stigmatized.
- **Curiosity** -- A desire to recover lost knowledge and innovate drives progress.
- **Faith** -- Religion is central to daily life. Brief prayers at household shrines are common.

### 8.2 Death & The Frontier
- Proximity to death shapes daily culture
- Grand festivals and plentiful food celebrate life
- **Memory shrines** with candles lit for the fallen are maintained in homes and public squares
- The frontier is viewed as both a source of fear and opportunity
- Fighters, adventurers and reconquerors are seen as a heroic class that does not demand but gets respect and admiration

### 8.3 Daily Religious Practice
- Brief prayers at household shrines
- Most common daily prayers: Light & Life (healing), Forge & Arcana (craft), Wealth & Fortune (luck)
- Larger observances at temples on festival days
### 8.4 Education
- **Public academies** (funded by guild taxes):
  - Basic (ages 6-12): Reading, writing, math, history, physical training
  - Apprenticeship (ages 12-18): Guild trade or military service
- **Higher education**:
  - Weaveheart Academy (mages)
  - Skywatch War College (officers)
  - Church seminaries (clerics, paladins)

#### Libraries
- **Grand Athenaeum** (Weaveheart): Arcane texts and historical records
- **Cartography Hall** (Skywatch): Maps and intelligence archives
- **Engineering Archives** (Emberforge): Schematics and metallurgical treatises

#### Lost Knowledge
- Approximately **70% of pre-invasion records** were destroyed
- Knowledge recovery is a respected profession
- Adventurers are often contracted to retrieve texts from monster-occupied sites

### 8.5 Arts & Entertainment
- **Music**: Skywatch Chorus (festival performances), Emberforge Operas (smithing + fire), Weaveheart Illuminations (magical light shows)
- **Literature**: Epic poems, practical manuals, scouting journals, religious texts
- **Games**: Strategy games, riddle contests, smithing competitions, archery tournaments

### 8.6 Social Structure
- Standing is earned through **concrete contributions to the reconquering**: monsters slain, territory reclaimed, communities protected
- No rigid caste system
- Reputation is local -- what matters varies by settlement
- Tensions exist between capital interests and frontier needs, between old pre-invasion family names and new merit

## 9. RACES & ANCESTRIES

### 9.1 Common Races

#### Humans
- Most populous race
- Created by **Aloria** (Light & Life)
- Lifespan: ~100 years
- Found everywhere across Kythoria
- Adaptable and ambitious; central to the reconquering effort
- Hold significant political power through the Church of Light and Life

#### Elves (High Elves and Wood Elves)
- Long-lived and nature-attuned
- Created by **Kaelthor** (Nature & Tempest)
- Lifespan: ~750 years
- High Elves: Arcane affinity, grace, longevity
- Wood Elves: Hardy, stealthy, deeply connected to forests
- Include two additional subraces: **Drow** and **Shadow Elves** (Shadar-kai)

#### Dwarves (Hill and Mountain)
- Master crafters and smiths
- Created by **Thalkis** (Forge & Arcana)
- Lifespan: ~350 years
- Central to Emberforge's industrial output
- Prominent in the Thalkis Ember  Guild

#### Halflings
- Known for luck and presence in trade and commerce
- Created by **Crassian** (Wealth & Fortune)
- Lifespan: ~250 years
- Well-liked and trusted across Kythoria
- Known as the continent's perfect accountants
- Their former capital Hearthglen housed the royal mint

#### Dragonborn
- Perfect hunters with draconic heritage
- Created by **Tyra** (Hunt & Nature)
- Lifespan: ~80 years
- Respected across Kythoria, especially on the frontier
- Draconic ancestry gives them breath weapons and damage resistance

#### Gnomes (Forest and Rock)
- Scholars and wisdom-keepers
- Created by **Aurelius** (Wisdom & Justice)
- Lifespan: ~500 years
- Forest Gnomes: Close to nature
- Rock Gnomes: Inventors and tinkerers
- Contribute to scholarship, law, and invention

#### Half-Elves
- Natural offspring of Elves and Humans

- Lifespan: ~200 years
- Natural diplomats and wanderers
- Generally accepted across Kythoria

#### Half-Orcs
- Natural offspring of interbreeding; 
- Orcs created by **Vorn** (War & Conquest)
- Lifespan: ~75 years
- Fought bravely in the First Alliance and helped found the Last Stand
- Yet face discrimination because Vorn is a banned god
- Mistrusted in nearly every settlement; seen as brutish and prone to violence
- Vorn worship among Half-Orcs must be conducted in secret

#### Tieflings

- Lifespan: ~100 years
- Face deep prejudice as "godless" or "abandoned"
- Often the first blamed for crimes
- Many have integrated into Last Stand society, proving worth through deeds


### 9.2 Uncommon Races

#### Genasi (Air, Earth, Fire, Water)

- Beings with connection to the Elemental Planes
- Created by **Vesper** (Peace & Twilight)
- Lifespan: ~120 years
- Rare but generally accepted
- Elemental nature viewed with curiosity rather than suspicion
- Subtypes: Air (connected to sky), Earth (stone and soil), Fire (flame and heat), Water (rivers and seas)

### 9.3 Races Summary

| Race         | God         | Social Standing                   |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| Humans       | Aloria      | Respected; politically powerful   |
| Elves        | Kaelthor    | Respected                         |
| Dwarves      | Thalkis     | Respected for craftsmanship       |
| Halflings    | Crassian    | Well-liked and trusted            |
| Dragonborn   | Tyra        | Respected, especially on frontier |
| Gnomes       | Aurelius    | Respected as scholars             |
| Half-Elves   | (none)      | Generally accepted                |
| Genasi       | Vesper      | Accepted, viewed with curiosity   |
| Half-Orcs    | Vorn (Orcs) | Mistrusted, discriminated against |
| Tieflings    | (none)      | Distrusted as "godless"           |
| Drow         | Lolth       | Highly distrusted, few on surface |
| Shadow Elves | Raven Queen | Distrusted, rare visitors         |

## 10. THE DROW AND SHADOW ELVES

### 10.1 Drow (Dark Elves)
- An elven subrace with sunlight sensitivity
- Created by **Lolth, the Spider Queen**
 
- Never participated in the First Alliance or helped found the Last Stand
- Viewed with deep suspicion in Last Stand territories

### 10.2 Shadow Elves (Shadar-kai)
- An elven subrace with a connection to the **Shadowfell**
- Created by the **Raven Queen**

- Primary worshippers of the Raven Queen

- Little is known about them
---

## 11. ECONOMY

### 11.1 Currency
Standard denominations recognized across all territories:
- **Copper Pieces (cp)** -- everyday transactions
- **Silver Pieces (sp)** -- standard wage and trade currency
- **Gold Pieces (gp)** -- high-value trade, magic items, large transactions
- **Platinum Pieces (pp)** -- extremely rare, used by major guilds and high-level commerce

### 11.2 The Royal Mint
- Located in the former **Kingdom of Hearthglen** (Halfling kingdom)
- Raw metals and gemstones from the northeast mining cluster are received, refined, and stamped into standard coinage
- Established before the monster invasion; resumed operations after the reconquering
- Remains the backbone of the continental economy

### 11.3 The Northeast Mining Cluster
- Located in the northeast of Kythoria
- Contains the greatest known mines for precious metals and gemstones
- Was part of the **Kingdom of Kazadur** (Dwarven kingdom) before the invasion
- Consists of one major settlement (**Kazadur**) and three minor ones:
  - A logistics hub where Halflings coordinate shipping
  - A mining town for currency metals
  - A mining town for gemstones
- Mining towns are open to any race wanting to earn coin

### 11.4 Major Industries

#### Mining & Prospecting
- The northeast cluster is the heart of mining operations
- Additional mines in the recovered south and east


#### Metalworking & Smithing
- **Emberforge** is the industrial heart of the mortal races
- Produces weapons, armor, tools, and arcane components
- Emberforge's technology is the most advanced on the continent
- Its weapons are considered the finest available

#### Agriculture
- Staple crops: grains (wheat, barley, oats), rice, exotic fruits, spices
- Livestock: cattle, sheep, poultry
- Food security is a strategic priority; granaries maintain siege reserves lasting years
- The forests in and surrounding the Last Stand are exceptionally fertile

#### Arcane Industry
- **House Thormvuld**: A dwarven arcane engineering family, the most prominent magical item producers on the continent
- They originate from the northeast region and own a dedicated settlement
- Recently built the floating estate **Seidga'ard**
- **Weaveheart** also produces high-quality enchanted equipment and trains spellcasters

#### Monster Hunting
- The continent-wide **Drakh Ix'thar** is the primary controller of this industry
- Settlements, caravans, and military outposts contract the guild for monster extermination and ruin clearance
- Monster parts are traded for alchemy, crafting, and arcane components

#### Military
- The Dawn Guard functions as a major military force, financed by the Last Stand
- Contracts local mercenary companies for specific operations
- These contracts inject significant coin into local economies

### 11.5 Trade Routes

#### Crassian's Dust Circle
- Ancient overland trade route predating the monster invasion
- Originally connected the six pre-invasion kingdoms
- Named after the great clouds of dust raised by caravans
- Restored during the reconquering; now connects most major settlements
- Remains the primary overland trade artery

#### The Eastern Sea Route
- Series of ports along the eastern coast connecting south to heartlands
- Ships carry goods north and south, stopping at waypoint towns
- Safer than land travel; handles the bulk of bulk trade


### 11.6 Major Exports
- **From the South**: Exotic fruits, spices, timber, rare herbs
- **From the Northeast**: Precious metals, gemstones, minted currency
- **From Emberforge**: Weapons, armor, industrial goods
- **From Weaveheart**: Enchanted items, magical components

### 11.7 Economic Challenges
- Resource scarcity -- many mines and forests remain under monster control
- Trade disruption -- monster attacks on caravans and ships still occur
- War economy inflation -- military production consumes civilian resources
- Black market -- underground trade in monster parts, illegal magical components, and contraband

---

## 12. MAGIC

### 12.1 The Arcane Weave
- The permeating field of magical energy that exists across all reality
- The source of all **arcane magic**
- Wizards study and manipulate the Weave through formulae, gestures, and components
- Sorcerers draw from it innately through bloodline or attunement
- The Weave is not uniform; **ley lines** are concentrated highways of magical energy

### 12.2 Three Paths of Magic
Public understanding recognizes three forms of magic:

| Path       | Source                                  | Classes                                    |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| **Arcane** | The Weave (studied or innate)           | Wizard, Sorcerer, Bard, Artificer, Warlock |
| **Divine** | Granted by the gods through prayer      | Cleric, Paladin                            |
| **Primal** | Drawn from nature's own absorbed energy | Druid, Ranger                              |

### 12.3 Divine Magic
- Clerics and paladins receive their powers from the gods
- Prayer is the mechanism by which divine favor is channeled
- Each god grants specific domains of magic to their faithful
- The god's power is believed to flow through the cleric

### 12.4 Primal Magic
- Druids, rangers, and some barbarians draw power from the natural world
- Nature itself is imbued with arcane energy
- Druids attune to the cycle of life, seasons, and living things
- Rangers draw from wild places and natural connection
- Barbarian rage is seen as channeling primal fury

### 12.5 Spell Components
- **Verbal & Somatic**: Words and gestures that shape magical energy
- **Material**: Physical components that serve as focal points; costly components are rare and consumed in casting

### 12.6 Ley Lines
- Invisible highways of concentrated arcane energy crisscrossing the world
- Magic is easier to channel near ley line convergences
- Areas far from ley lines may feel magically impoverished
- Weaveheart is built at a major convergence

### 12.7 Magical Items
- Enchanted weapons, armor, and tools are highly valued
- **House Thormvuld** is the premier producer of magical items
- **Weaveheart Academy** also produces enchanted equipment
- Magical items recovered from pre-invasion ruins and monster nests are highly sought after

### 12.8 Arcane-Reactive Crystals (Recent Discovery)
- Rumors, whispers, and gossip about these crystals have begun circulating among the public
- A heist was reportedly pulled on the floating island by two coordinated parties
- House Thormvuld claims nothing too valuable was stolen

- Much of the public has only heard rumors of "strange crystals"

---

## 13. ADVENTURING CLASSES

### 13.1 Class Overview

| Class         | Power Source                                 | Public Perception                                       |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Artificer** | Weave manipulation through craft             | Highly respected; valued in Emberforge & frontier       |
| **Barbarian** | Primal fury; survival instinct               | Respected warrior tradition; four great tribes          |
| **Bard**      | Innate arcane + Weave; expressed through art | Highly respected history-keepers and diplomats          |
| **Cleric**    | Divine channeling through prayer             | Pillars of communities; deeply trusted                  |
| **Druid**     | Primal attunement to nature                  | Respected; essential on the frontier                    |
| **Fighter**   | Pure martial discipline                      | Backbone of the military; common and respected          |
| **Monk**      | Inner Ki discovered through meditation       | Rare; viewed with curiosity and respect                 |
| **Paladin**   | Oath to a god; power through conviction      | Respected holy warriors; military arm of faith          |
| **Ranger**    | Primal attunement + martial skill            | Essential for survival; deeply respected                |
| **Rogue**     | Skill, stealth, and cunning                  | Feared, distrusted, but acknowledged as essential       |
| **Sorcerer**  | Innate bloodline connection                  | Curiosity mixed with mistrust (power they did not earn) |
| **Warlock**   | Pact with an external entity                 | Mistrust and fear-respect (unknown patrons)             |
| **Wizard**    | Weave study and precision                    | Respected in Weaveheart; scholarly elite                |



### 13.2 Training Institutions

| Institution                           | Location     | Trains                                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts** | Weaveheart   | Wizards, Sorcerers (supplementary), Bards (supplementary) |
| **Skywatch War College**              | Skywatch     | Fighters, Paladins, Rangers, strategic officers           |
| **Emberforge Engineering Halls**      | Emberforge   | Artificers                                                |
| **Church Seminaries**                 | All capitals | Clerics, Paladins (religious education)                   |
| **Guiding Hand' Guild**          | Skywatch     | Rangers, Rogues (scout path)                              |

### 13.4 Informal Training Paths
- **Apprenticeship**: Most common path (blacksmiths teach artificers, veterans teach fighters)
- **Tribal tradition**: Barbarians (four tribes), some Druids
- **Self-taught**: Sorcerers, some Rogues
- **Wandering master**: Monks (rare post-invasion), some Bards
- **Pact-based**: Warlocks (power granted directly by patron)

### 13.5 The Last Stand Army Composition
- **Frontline**: Fighter, Paladin, Barbarian, Monk
- **Support**: Cleric, Druid, Ranger
- **Arcane Corps**: Wizard, Artificer
- **Rare in army**: Sorcerer, Warlock, Rogue

## 14. THE ADVENTURERS' GUILD (DRAKH IX'THAR)

### 14.1 Overview
- **Name**: Drakh Ix'thar -- "The Great Dragon Hunt" in Draconic
- Members are called **Ix'tharian** (singular: Ix'thari)
- A continent-wide organization predating the monster invasion
- Survived the Abominable End and was re-established during the reconquering
- Headquarters in **Drakhaven** at the center of the continent
- Chapter houses exist in every major settlement

### 14.2 Purpose
The guild serves as:
- **Contract broker**: Connecting parties with settlements needing monster extermination, ruin clearance, or frontier scouting
- **Licensing & certification**: Ensuring minimum competence and accountability
- **Information network**: Sharing intelligence about frontier conditions and monster movements
- **Support system**: Providing healing, equipment repair, safe lodging, and resupply

### 14.3 Membership
- Open to adventurers of all classes
- Ranks are named in Draconic after legendary beasts
- Advance based on successful contracts and contribution to the reconquering
- Highest rank: **Drah Ix'thari** (Dragon Hunter)
- Higher ranks unlock access to more dangerous contracts, restricted zones, and greater guild resources

### 14.4 Economic Role
- Clearing monster nests makes land safe for settlement
- Recovering treasure from pre-invasian/monster-occupied ruins
- Gathering frontier intelligence
- Field-testing prototype weapons from Emberforge

### 14.5 History
- Founded long before the Abominable End as a guild of monster hunters serving the six kingdoms
- Suspended operations in Year 134 when the capital of Kythoria fell to the monster invasion
- Many members fought alongside the First Alliance
- Re-established during the reconquering with headquarters in Drakhaven restored

### 14.6 Adventurers in Society
- Adventurers are seen as **guardians, cleansers, and reclaimers** -- not mere mercenaries
- They handle threats beyond city walls, clear ruins, and recover artifacts
- The profession carries immense honor and respect
- Adventurers are seen as a heroic class in Kythorian society

---

## 15. MONSTERS & THE INVASION

### 15.1 The Monster Threat

#### Origins
- Approximately **400 years ago**, monsters began appearing at the fringes of Kythoria
- Their origins remain **unknown** to the general public
- The numbers were relentless; they pushed inward, consuming territory
- For two centuries, they drove the mortal races before them

#### Types of Monsters
- **Invasion Monsters**: Creatures that appeared during the Abominable End. Diverse in form and ability. Specific types vary across regions.
- **Native Monsters**: Magical beasts that existed on Kythoria before the invasion: dragons, owlbears, basilisks, manticores, griffons, and similar creatures. These are not allied with the invasion forces.
- **Crystal-Corrupted**: Monsters with visible crystal growths protruding from their bodies, enhanced durability, and strange behavior. Poorly understood.


### 15.2 The Five Generals (Historical)
- By the time the Last Stand was founded (~200 years ago), the monster army had consolidated under **Five Major Generals**
- The most powerful and cunning creatures to emerge from the invasion
- The First Alliance defeated **three of the Five Generals**
- The other two generals retreated and have not been seen since
- The five generals' identities are unknown to the public


### 15.3 Current Monster Threat
- With no new monsters arriving, those already on Kythoria remain devastating
- The **Frozen North** is still largely monster-held
- Several monster groups now seem to operate semi-independently, unity seems fractured within the mosnter army
- Approximately **one-third of the continent** remains under monster control

---

## 16. NOTABLE ORGANIZATIONS

### 16.1 The Seven Recognized Churches

#### Order of the Dawn (Aloria -- Light & Life)
- Most politically powerful church
- Temples in all settlements; main temple in Weaveheart
- Clergy: Healers, midwives, protectors, paladins
- Runs hospices, tends the sick, stands as  shinning beacon of hope

#### Guild of the Spark (Thalkis -- Forge & Arcana)
- Combines church with craft guild
- Temples are workshops, forges, and arcane libraries
- Main temple in Emberforge
- Strong ties to Emberforge's smithing traditions
- Clergy: Smith-priests, enchanters, artificers

#### Circle of the Wild (Kaelthor -- Nature & Tempest)
- Loose affiliation of druids, rangers, and weather-watchers
- No centralized hierarchy; no single headquarters
- Most important sites are ancient groves, sacred mountains, and wild places
- The world itself is considered the only true temple

#### Order of the Scales (Aurelius -- Wisdom & Justice)
- Temples double as libraries, courts, and academies
- Main temple in Weaveheart
- Clergy: Judges, scholars, diplomats, lawkeepers
- Preserves pre-invasion knowledge; advises rulers on legal matters

#### Order of the Currency (Crassian -- Wealth & Fortune)
- Temples double as banks and marketplaces
- Main temple in Drakhaven; strong presence in all capitals
- Clergy: Traders, moneylenders, advisors on risky ventures
- Connected to the Mint and major trade guilds

#### Vigil of the Dusk (Vesper -- Peace & Twilight)
- Quiet, contemplative presence
- Temples are sanctuaries of peace
- Main temple in Weaveheart
- Clergy: Diplomats, hospice workers, gatekeepers, mediators

#### Pack of Tyra (Tyra -- Hunt & Nature)
- Most decentralized of the recognized churches
- Organized into loose hunting bands called "packs"
- No single headquarters; seasonal Great Hunt at rotating frontier location
- Clergy: Hunters, survivalists, game wardens, trappers


### 16.2 The First Alliance
- The unprecedented military and political alliance of the mortal races

- Defeated three of the Five Monster Generals
- Continues to oversee the reconquering effort
- Membership includes all recovered settlements, knightly orders and major guilds

### 16.4 The Council Accord
- The governing body of the three capitals (see Section 5.1)
- The highest authority in mortal civilization
- Coordinates military strategy, resource allocation, and territorial expansion

### 16.5 The Ecumenical Council
- Interfaith body representing the seven recognized churches (see Section 6.5)
- Mediates disputes, coordinates festivals, presents unified religious front

### 16.6 House Thormvuld
- Dwarven arcane engineering dynasty
- Most prominent magical item producers on the continent
- Originate from the northeast mining region
- Built the floating estate **Seidga'ard** 
- Recently subject to a high-profile heist on their floating estate
- Ruthless, authoritarian house; currently hunting the thieves
- **Lord Keylor Thormvuld** is the patriarch


### 16.7 The Venom-Weavers
- A prolific assassin guild specializing in poisons and knife combat
- Operate in the shadows of major settlements and throughout the frontier
- Not aligned with any faction; serve whoever pays
- One of the most feared and respected underworld organizations
- Led by **Rhael**; organized into a hierarchy of skill and trust

---

## 17. NOTABLE LOCATIONS

### 17.1 The Six Fallen Capitals

#### Drakhaven (Human)
- Former capital of the Human kingdom; largest and most advanced pre-invasion city
- Self-appointed "capital of Kythoria"
- Located at the center of the continent
- Seat of the Drakh Ix'thar (Adventurers' Guild) and the High Septon (central temple of Aurelius)
- Partially reclaimed; guild headquarters and High Septon restored

#### Elyndor (Elven)
- Former capital of the Elven kingdom; ancient forest city of arcane knowledge
- City blended seamlessly with the natural landscape around a sacred grove
- Fell to the monster invasion; ruins remain in monster-held territory

#### Kazadur (Dwarven)
- Former capital of the Dwarven kingdom in the northeast
- Mountain-forge capital; greatest mines on the continent
- Before the fall, the dwarven king sealed the deep halls and collapsed the tunnels
- Mines partially reclaimed; sealed halls remain undiscovered
- Survivors' blueprints and knowledge led to Emberforge's establishment

#### Hearthglen (Halfling)
- Former capital of the Halfling kingdom; economic heart of the continent
- Home of the royal mint and the continent's perfect accountants
- Annihilated by the monster army; fields salted, granaries looted, every building burned
- The valley remains scarred; small halfling communities have re-established elsewhere

#### Everquill (Gnome)
- Former capital of the Gnome kingdom; the paper capital of law, records, and maps
- When the city fell, gnome archivists fled with records of all six kingdoms
- Much of what the Last Stand knows about the pre-invasion era was carried from Everquill
- Ruins stand in monster-held territory; the Great Archive's lower vaults may have survived

#### Stonefist (Half-Orc)
- Former capital of the Half-Orc kingdom; rugged fortress of proud warriors
- Ruins remain in monster-held territory
- Half-Orc survivors carried martial traditions to the First Alliance

### 17.2 Settlements

#### Stonefall
- Practical frontier town on the edge of Last Stand territory
- Timber and stone construction; population of a few dozens
- Last real settlement before the wilderness
- Trading post for frontier goods and resting point for expeditions
- Features a half-finished wall, a tavern, market square, shrine to Aurelius, and blacksmith

#### The Southeastern Port
- Major sea trade hub in the southeast
- Heavily fortified, coastal, highly defensible
- One of the main maritime commerce centers

#### The Eastern Port
- Additional sea connection on the eastern coast
- Fishing, trade, and travel hub



### 17.3 The High Septon
- Central temple of Aurelius in Drakhaven

- Where paladins swear their oaths before Aurelius

## 18. RECENT EVENTS (Year 500 -- Campaign Start)


### 18.1 The Heist on Seidga'ard
- A coordinated two-party group infiltrated House Thormvuld's floating estate
- One party gathered intelligence disguised as catering staff
- A second party entered under diplomatic cover as ambassadors of the Dark Alliance
- Crystals, schematics, and prototype devices were reportedly stolen
- House Thormvuld claims nothing too valuable was taken
- House Thormvuld is actively hunting the perpetrators
- Details remain murky; public knowledge is based on rumors and gossip

### 18.3 The Dark Alliance
- Drow and Shadow Elves have formed a new political alliance
- Knowledge of this alliance is only recently spreading

### 18.4 State of the Reconquering
- Three-quarters of the continent has been reclaimed
- Population numbers back to approximately 60% of pre-invasion values
- Economy is functional; food growth is stable; political situation is balanced
- Strong cooperation between races
- Hardest contest remains on the north and north-west
- The reconquering endures

---

## 19. COMMON EXPRESSIONS & CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE

### 19.1 Sayings & Proverbs
- "Divided we fight but united we stand" -- core ethos of the Last Stand
- "The world is the only true temple" -- Circle of the Wild teaching
- A city's strength is measured by its contributions to the reconquering

### 19.2 Common Knowledge Points

- Drakhaven's humans called their city the "capital of Kythoria" -- a boast other races accepted with a smirk
- Halflings are considered the continent's perfect accountants
- Emberforge weapons are the finest available
- The magical barrier has held for two centuries; few people alive remember the world without it
- The Day of Silence is the only day no one works and no magic is cast
- The Drakh Ix'thar guild predates the monster invasion
- ~70% of pre-invasion knowledge has been lost
- Crassian's Dust Circle is named after the great clouds of dust raised by caravans
---

## END OF MASTER PUBLIC LORE

This document represents the boundary of what an average, educated citizen of Kythoria would know about their world at the start of the campaign.
